mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1600 units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of instances when HOUST > 1600, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 5.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shows a 3-month average growth rate above 200k, the tightening labor market leads to increased wage pressures, driving inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, indicating supply chain disruptions, leads to decreased earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of supply disruptions on earnings
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when INDPRO < 6-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Robust growth in real disposable income (RSAFS), above 5% YoY, fuels increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during the holiday season (Oct-Dec).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of holiday season instances when RSAFS growth > 5% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5%, signaling monetary tightening, leads to decreased equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, but only when accompanied by rising inflation expectations (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY).
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with rising inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (not available in the provided catalog, using PAYEMS as a proxy for labor market health), above a 3-month average growth rate of -50k, signals labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market distress impacts on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3% YoY, indicating strong aggregate demand, drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, but this effect is muted during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 > 3% YoY and CPIAUCSL < 3% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
